findings.title: fire_unit_until cannot stop a firing early because mt-run blocks until the unit exits
findings.description:
`fire_unit_until` calls `run(["mt-run", *mt_run_args], sudo=True, check=False, stream=True)` and only afterwards calls `wait_for_unit_or_line` (line 357). `deploy/mt-run` does not return while the unit runs. `start_and_stream` issues `systemctl start --no-block` (deploy/mt-run:127), then loops `while is_running "${unit}"; do sleep 2; done` (line 129). `subprocess.run` therefore blocks for the whole unbounded firing. By the time the trailing-line check runs, the unit has ended, so `reached and unit_active(unit)` (line 358) is false and `stop_unit` never runs. The cutover still waits for the full backfill, which is the problem #22 was meant to fix.

The test `test_the_minute_firing_stops_once_the_trailing_phase_completes` mocks `run` and `unit_active`, so it cannot detect this. Fix: start the unit directly with `sudo systemctl start --no-block <unit>` (already allowed by `MT_UNITS`) and poll with `wait_for_unit_or_line`. Add a test that asserts the start call does not block.

findings.title: The sudoers rule grants root execution of a script the operator account can rewrite
findings.description:
`MT_INSTALL` lets `manta` run `/home/manta/source/repos/manta/trading-data/deploy/install-production.sh --ref *` as root with NOPASSWD. That file is in the operator's own checkout, which is what `install()` resolves (scripts/cutover_common.py:134). The account that runs the scripts can rewrite that file and then execute it as root, which is a root shell in one step. The header's "limited root" claim does not hold. I did not verify the file owner on the host; the conclusion assumes the checkout is writable by `manta`, which the `/home/manta` layout implies.

Fix: install a root-owned copy outside the checkout (for example under `/usr/local/sbin`, updated by root from a pinned ref) and grant NOPASSWD on that path only. Alternatively, drop the NOPASSWD entry and keep the password prompt for the installer.

findings.title: The sudoers rule does not match what the scripts actually run
findings.description: The header says the rule covers "exactly the commands those scripts issue". But `_repair` runs `sudo /opt/manta-trading/.venv/bin/python scripts/repair_921_minute_sessions.py <mode>`, and no rule covers that interpreter. Each repair and verify call falls back to a password prompt, and `sudo -n` fails. The installer path also disagrees: `install()` resolves it from `__file__` (scripts/cutover_common.py:134), while the rule hard-codes one checkout path, so running from any other checkout (including a worktree) prompts for a password. Add the interpreter, narrowly, for this script's three modes. Either pin the installer location or document that the checkout must match.

findings.title: MT_RUN wildcard exposes the whole production mt CLI to root
findings.description: `/usr/local/bin/mt-run *` matches any arguments. Non-verb arguments go to `run_production_mt` (deploy/mt-run:160-168). When run as root, that function sources `/etc/manta-trading.env` and `exec`s `/opt/manta-trading/.venv/bin/mt "$@"` as root. The cutover scripts need only `mt-run minute`, `mt-run daily`, `mt-run kalshi`, and `mt-run data kalshi status --json`. Narrow the rule to those invocations.

findings.title: Ctrl-C does not leave the script waiting; it aborts it and restarts the timers
findings.description: The printed text "Ctrl-C only detaches, the script keeps waiting" is not true for the Python process. Nothing in `cutover_common` installs a SIGINT handler, so Ctrl-C raises `KeyboardInterrupt` inside `subprocess.run`, which kills the `mt-run` child and unwinds `main()`. The unwind runs `finally: _release_timers(held)` (scripts/cutover_921_minute_sessions.py:274-275), which restarts the minute and daily timers while the unit may still be running. The same wording exists in the pre-existing `fire()` and `fire_unit()`, but `fire_unit_until` copies it. Catch the interrupt around the firing and wait for the unit (or keep the timers held) instead of releasing them.

findings.title: The narration log omits the acceptance output it is meant to record
findings.description: Only `say()` lines are teed into the log file (scripts/cutover_common.py:57-62). The file is described as "the cutover's report" and, at exit, as the "full narration". But `_repair` writes the repair output with `print(output)` (line 102), and the sub-step lines in `cutover_common` (wait loops, sudo prompts, streamed `mt-run` output) also bypass `say()`. The `[PASS]`/`[FAIL]`/`[WAIT]` lines that decide the exit code are therefore absent from the file. Route `_repair`'s output through `say`, or drop the "full narration" wording.

findings.title: The cagg freshness probe duplicates the refresh-job query and drops its '-infinity' guard
findings.description: `cagg_freshness_for_session` re-spells the refresh-job lookup that `market/maintenance/cagg_freshness.py` already has as `_JOB_SQL` and `_read_refresh_job` (lines 73-83 and 270-313). The existing query normalizes `last_successful_finish = '-infinity'` to NULL, and the module's own comment (cagg_freshness.py:68-72) says psycopg raises `DataError` on that value. The new copy selects the raw column, so a refresh policy that has never finished makes `--verify` raise instead of reporting. Share the lookup rather than copying it.

findings.title: The truncated-day fix reaches the seed only on some daemon code paths
findings.description: `uncovered_days` only takes effect inside `if seed_from is not None` (line 752). `seed_from` is set when the symbol has UNKNOWN gap rows (full seed, lines 738-739) or when the gap frontier `MAX(gap_end)` trails `target_end` (lines 740-750). In the frontier case the seed covers only sessions at or after the frontier. A truncated session older than the newest gap row, on a symbol with no UNKNOWN rows, is never passed to the seed. That contradicts the docstring of `_build_truncated_index` (minute.py:355-363), which says truncated sessions are re-seeded. The only forwarding test, `test_do_minute_symbol_forwards_uncovered_days_to_the_seed`, forces `has_unknown_gaps=True`, so it covers only the full-seed branch. Add a frontier-branch test with an older truncated day, then either change the seed decision or document the limit. I did not check this against production data.

findings.title: The daemon now depends on the slice-921 repair module
findings.description: The steady-state daemon imports `build_truncated_day_index` and `RepairScanTimeout` from `data/gaps/repair_921.py`, a module written as a one-off slice repair. Retiring slice 921 would leave the daemon depending on repair tooling. Move the truncated-day index and its predicate into a shared gaps module that both the daemon and the repair import.

findings.title: The 04:05 firing rationale is wrong for standard time, which is the current period
findings.description: The comment says 20:00 ET is 00:00 UTC and that 04:05 "leaves an hour over the provider's upper bound". That holds only on daylight time. DST ended 2026-11-01, so ET is UTC-5 now. 20:00 ET is then 01:00 UTC, two to three hours later is 03:00–04:00 UTC, and 04:05 leaves about five minutes. The cited measurement is from 2026-09-10 (EDT). Restate the margin in UTC for both offsets. An early firing is limited by the design, since a spillover-only session stays PARTIAL and is retried at 13:05, consuming one of `MAX_RETRY_COUNT` = 5 attempts (constants.py:69). So this is a documentation and margin problem, not data loss.

findings.title: Verify verdict markers are scattered across two scripts
findings.description: The verdict protocol between `repair_921_minute_sessions.py` (which prints `[WAIT]`, `[FAIL]`, `[PASS]`) and the cutover is a substring match on literals. `"[WAIT]"` appears at cutover lines 204, 265, and 273, and in the repair's print at repair_921_minute_sessions.py:288. CLAUDE.md says a comparison value used in conditionals must be defined once. Define the markers as constants in one module and build both the printed lines and the checks from them. A changed spelling in the repair would currently make `"[WAIT]" in text` silently false and the cutover would accept.

findings.title: The timer comment still describes the old stagger
findings.description: "Staggered 30 minutes behind mt-daily-pass.timer" was true when the minute pass fired at 01:05. At 04:05 against the daily 00:35 the gap is 3.5 hours. Only the 13:05/12:35 pair is 30 minutes apart. The "never start simultaneously" intent still holds, but the stated number is wrong.

findings.title: Bar presence cannot separate "not yet published" from "no bars", and the judgment accepts one bar
findings.description: The info log asserts "provider has not published them; row kept". The code cannot tell that apart from a session the provider has no bars for, such as a halted or thinly traded name. Such a chunk stays PARTIAL, each attempt re-fetches the chunk at full call cost, and the row becomes RETRY_EXHAUSTED after `MAX_RETRY_COUNT` attempts (minute.py:1147-1151). That is bounded, not a loop, but the log states a cause the code does not know. Reword it to "no bars in session(s)". Separately, `sessions_without_bars` counts a session as collected on any single bar after its open. That matches the repair's truncated-day predicate, but a fetch that stops one minute after the open passes. Say so in the docstring.

findings.title: Cagg freshness compares timestamps that are not ordered the way the probe assumes
findings.description: `minute_ohlcv.created_at` defaults to `NOW()` (market/schema/migrations/minute.py:797), which is the start of the writing transaction. The refresh is compared at `last_successful_finish`, not at the job's start. A refresh whose snapshot predates a concurrent chunk commit can read as fresh. The cutover holds the timers, so this is unlikely during verify, but the guarantee only holds for a quiescent database. Compare against the job's start time, which is more conservative.

findings.title: Each trailing cycle runs a universe-wide scan that was not measured here
findings.description: `_build_truncated_index` calls `build_truncated_day_index` with no symbol filter on every trailing cycle. The scan is bounded by `since=trailing_floor` and a 600 s statement timeout (repair_921.py:50, 265), and a timeout is logged. The repair's 7.9 s figure was measured over six weeks on production, not over the trailing window. Measure it against the trailing window before relying on it in the daemon.

findings.title: Import order does not match ruff's isort rule
findings.description: By inspection, the new imports break ruff's I001. `daemon.minute_sessions` and `data.gaps.compute_missing_ranges` sort ahead of `data.gaps`, and `repair_921` sorts ahead of `minute_coverage`. The cutover import (scripts/cutover_921_minute_sessions.py:45-58) and the repair imports list functions ahead of classes. The file already had ordering violations before this diff (lines 28-29), so `ruff check` is not clean here. I could not run ruff to confirm.

findings.title: A pre-existing bare-catch sits directly above the new session judgment
findings.description: This code is outside the hunk, so it is pre-existing: `except Exception: bars = []` swallows any `.json()` failure with no log. This diff now feeds that result into `judge_chunk_by_sessions`. The `response_carries_an_answer` gate makes this rare. Still, the rule requires re-raising or handling a named exception, so narrow it to `ValueError` and log it.

findings.title: The chunk-judgment tests repeat the same setup
findings.description: `_run` and `test_last_bar_before_the_chunk_end_is_still_success` each repeat about 40 lines of identical pool, transaction, lock, and patch setup. `TestTruncatedDayAwareSeeding` repeats the same block again. Extract one helper that takes bounds, gap, and bars.

findings.title: minute.py is far past the file-size guideline and this diff adds to it
findings.description: The file runs past 1,300 lines (`_insert_minute_bars` starts at line 1291), against the ~300-line guideline in CLAUDE.md. The diff adds about 60 more. This is not a blocker, but the trailing, backfill, seed, and judgment logic would be easier to change as separate modules.
